system.name: LinkLab 2.0
system.one_liner: a multi-tenant, three-layer (IoT/edge/cloud) programmable IoT testbed for experimenting with edge-cloud integration

components.name: Applications
components.role: top layer where user experiments and their data run

components.name: Database
components.role: data storage services available to experiments (InfluxDB, Redis, MySQL)

components.name: Experimental Applications
components.role: user application runtimes available for experiments

components.name: LinkLab Edge/Cloud Runtime
components.role: LinkLab's own runtime layer supporting programming, controlling, and monitoring of edge/cloud devices

components.name: Provision
components.role: services for deploying and configuring experiments on a device

components.name: LDC Client
components.role: agent connecting the device to the LDC management plane

components.name: Service Manager
components.role: manages the lifecycle of services/applications on the device

components.name: Exe. Support
components.role: execution support services for running experiments on the device

components.name: Router Agent
components.role: routes traffic/data for the running experiment

components.name: Connector
components.role: connects the runtime to external systems/services

components.name: Data Collection
components.role: collects operational data from the device for monitoring

components.name: KubeEdge
components.role: underlying open-source edge-computing platform that LinkLab's runtime is built on

content.key_idea: LinkLab's edge/cloud devices run a three-layer software stack: KubeEdge at the base, LinkLab's own Provision/Execution-Support/Data-Collection runtime in the middle, and user experiments (serverless functions, Docker apps, databases) on top.
content.reading_order: Bottom-up: KubeEdge is the foundation, the LinkLab Edge/Cloud Runtime's three columns (Provision, Exe. Support, Data Collection) sit above it, and Applications run on top.

summary: This figure shows the software stack running on each of LinkLab 2.0's programmable edge/cloud devices. At the base sits KubeEdge, the open-source edge-computing platform the stack is built on. On top of it, LinkLab's own Edge/Cloud Runtime (outlined in red) provides three parallel groups of services: Provision (LDC Client, Config. Manager, Service Manager) for deploying and configuring experiments; Exe. Support (Func. Runtime, Router Agent, Connector) for running them; and Data Collection (Data Logging, Sys. Monitoring, NTP) for observing them. At the top, an Applications layer (purple) hosts the actual experiments: a Database group offering InfluxDB, Redis, and MySQL, and Experimental Applications that can run as Serverless Functions or Docker-based apps. No arrows are drawn; the three dashed, color-coded boxes are simply stacked to show what runs on top of what.
